title: Meat substitute, cereal- and vegetable protein-based, fried

content.title: About
content.content: The meat substitute, cereal- and vegetable protein-based, fried, is a plant‑based protein product made from a blend of cereals (wheat, rice, corn) and vegetable proteins (soy, pea). It is fried to a golden crust, giving a crunchy texture and a flavor reminiscent of traditional meat snacks.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The product is completely vegan and contains no animal ingredients.
Cereal and legume proteins are combined to provide a complete amino‑acid profile comparable to meat.
Frying is done with minimal oil, preserving crunch while keeping calories lower.
It is often used in vegetarian and vegan versions of dishes, replacing patties, nuggets, and sticks.
Fiber content is higher than most meat analogues, supporting digestion.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Provides 15–20 % protein, helping maintain muscle mass and satiety.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Most fats are polyunsaturated, beneficial for cardiovascular health.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids gut function and helps stabilize blood sugar levels.

items.title: B‑vitamin complex
items.content: Fortified with thiamine, riboflavin, and niacin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Cholesterol‑free
items.content: Contains no cholesterol, making it safe for people with elevated lipid levels.

items.title: Soy and pea protein allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to soy or pea may experience reactions, up to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Gluten content
items.content: If wheat is used, the product is not suitable for those with celiac disease.

items.title: Salt and additives
items.content: Some versions may contain higher sodium or flavor enhancers, which should be considered in a restricted diet.

items.title: Processed ingredients
items.content: As with many ready‑made foods, it may contain preservatives; choose options without artificial additives when possible.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The product can be enjoyed as a snack, added to salads, vegetarian burgers, soups, or used as a coating for vegetables. For best texture, reheat in the oven or skillet until crisp.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place in a sealed package. After opening, consume within 2–3 days or keep refrigerated for up to a week. Discard if a rancid odor develops.
